# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this

# Allow drag and drop from the hand

**Headline:** Hand-held businesses (and "possibly other cards") will not drag
to the play area. The producer reproduced this on a **local dev server** with
the tutorial off and actions remaining, in **Edge** — so this is a live defect
in the dev build, not a stale release: the hand-drag feature
(`MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0`) is present in `dev` source but does not engage for the
player. Event cards are confirmed **click-only** by the producer. The job is to
reproduce on `dev`, root-cause, fix, and pin the behaviour with a regression
test that survives a scene refresh.

## Problem statement

> Seed report (producer): “Businesses, and possibly other cards, cannot be
> dragged and dropped from the hand to the play area.”

The market row drags to play in one gesture; the same gesture on a card that
has moved into the hand does nothing in the producer's local dev build. The
hand-drag implementation (`MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0`, committed to `dev` as
`a447c0b7`) registers hand containers as `@ui/dragDrop` draggables and has
passing browser tests, so the failure is in a path those tests do not cover —
most plausibly a **refresh-cycle interaction**: `refreshMarket()` calls
`unregisterDragDraggables()` (which clears every registered draggable,
hand-origin ones included) and the hand is only re-registered when
`refreshPlayerHand()` runs afterwards in the same cycle. Any refresh path that
rebuilds or unregisters without re-rendering the hand leaves live hand cards
unregistered, so the pointer never starts a drag.

## Users

- **The player (human seat).** Single-player and the human seat in competitive
  play share the same hand input paths.

User stories:

- *As a player, I want to drag a business card from my hand onto an empty
  street slot so I can place it without the select-then-click two-step.*
- *As a player, I want the gesture I learn on the market row to keep working
  after a card has moved into my hand — including after I buy, sell or place
  something else.*
- *As a player, I want to know that event cards are played by clicking, so I do
  not read the missing drag as a bug.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction captured on `dev`.** A comment records the served checkout
   (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD`), browser
   (Edge, as reported), tutorial state (skipped/off) and actions remaining,
   plus the result of attempting a hand→street drag for a **business**,
   a **community-space** and an **upgrade** card. The reproduction must include
   a drag attempted both **immediately at turn start** and **after another
   action that triggers a scene refresh** (buy from market, sell, place, end
   turn), since the refresh path is the prime suspect.
2. **Root cause identified with evidence.** The failure is attributed to a
   specific code path (drag registration, refresh ordering, pointer hit-test,
   or browser input) and the attribution is backed by observable evidence —
   e.g. the hand container's `input`/draggable state and the
   `renderer.dragDropRegistered` membership at the moment of the failed drag —
   recorded on the work item. If the served checkout turns out to predate
   `a447c0b7`, that is recorded as the explanation instead, with the commit
   hashes proving it.
3. **Fix: hand drag works on `dev` for businesses, community-space and upgrade
   cards.** With the tutorial off and at least one action remaining, each of
   those families drags from the hand to a legal street target and resolves
   through the existing undoable commands (`playBusinessFromHandCommand` /
   `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`), with no action or coins spent on an illegal
   drop. Pure clicks still reach `onHandBusinessCardClick` /
   `onHandUpgradeCardClick` (drag-vs-click coexistence preserved).
4. **Refresh safety.** Drag registration survives every refresh path
   (`refreshAll`, `refreshAllExceptStreet`, and mid-turn partial refreshes):
   after each, hand cards remain draggable. The fix must not rely on a single
   render ordering; a guard (or an explicit re-registration step) makes the
   invariant hold by construction.
5. **Event cards stay click-only (producer-confirmed).** Hand-held event cards
   are not registered as draggables and keep the select-then-act `[Play]` /
   `[Discard]` flow; a test pins this so a future family-wide registration
   change cannot silently make them draggable.
6. **Regression tests.** Browser test coverage exercises a hand→street drag
   **after a scene refresh cycle** (the uncovered path), and a unit-level test
   covers the registration invariant directly. Assertions go through the
   scene's public interaction surface and resulting state — never source greps.
7. **Docs.** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` hand-drag section states the
   supported hand families (business, community-space, upgrade) and that event
   cards are click-only; the refresh/registration invariant is documented in
   the code comment where it is enforced.
8. **Testing/validation.** The changed-scope test gate passes, and the new
   tests fail against the unfixed code (they genuinely reproduce the defect).
9. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Reuse the existing infrastructure:** the `@ui/dragDrop` manager, the street
  drop zones, the shared `dragHighlightRects` pool, `canPickUpHandCard` /
  `canDropHandCard`, and the undoable from-hand commands. No new engine state
  or action types.
- **Market-row drag behaviour is unchanged** (including the +50 % buy-and-play
  premium, which does not apply to hand-origin drags).
- **Do not regress the published build story:** `main`@`89118a84` (`v0.1.21`)
  still predates `a447c0b7`, so the published site also lacks the gesture. This
  item fixes the dev defect; shipping to `main` remains a producer-authorised
  ship-skill action, not part of this item.
- **Event cards are out of drag scope** — the producer has decided they stay
  click-only.
- **Browser matrix:** Edge (Chromium) is the reported browser; the headless
  Chromium browser tests are the executable proxy. Any Edge-only behaviour change
  must be called out explicitly.
- Investigation and code use **UK English**; all agent-initiated test runs go
  through the test skill.

## Existing state

- `dev` HEAD `19953f60`: hand containers are registered as draggables in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`renderCard` → both the upgrade and
  the business/community-space branches call `s.dragDropManager.registerDraggable`
  with `hitArea`, `canPickUp: canPickUpHandCard`, and the hand drop handlers).
  Drop-zone `canAccept` and the highlight resolver in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` resolve the dragged id from the
  hand first, then the market.
- Refresh cycle (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` `refreshAll`):
  `refreshStreetGrid` → `refreshMarket` → `refreshIncidentQueue` →
  **`refreshPlayerHand`**. `refreshMarket` starts with
  `renderer.unregisterDragDraggables()` (`MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`), which
  unregisters **every** tracked draggable — market *and* hand — and clears
  `renderer.dragDropRegistered`. Only the subsequent `refreshPlayerHand` →
  `handView.setCards()` → `rebuildDisplay()` → `renderCard` re-registers hand
  cards. The invariant therefore depends on render ordering, not on the drag
  manager.
- `refreshAllExceptStreet` (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts`) has the same ordering:
  `refreshMarket` (unregister) → `refreshPlayerHand` (re-register).
- Existing tests: `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts` — they drag shortly after boot;
  none exercises a drag after an action-triggered refresh.
- Docs (dev only): `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Hand-drag gesture:
  upgrades and business cards (MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0)".
- `main`@`89118a84` (2026-10-16, `v0.1.21`) has no hand-drag registration at
  all, and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` publishes `main` only.

## Desired change

- A reproduced, evidenced root cause for "hand cards will not drag" on `dev`.
- Hand→street drag that works for business, community-space and upgrade cards
  in the market phase, including after any refresh-triggering action.
- Drag registration that cannot be silently dropped by a later refresh (or a

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — `unregisterDragDraggables`

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshAll` /

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts` — `canPickUpHandCard`,

- `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` /

```bash

git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse --short HEAD
git log --oneline -1 --grep='MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0'

```

Then, in Edge with the tutorial off and at least one action remaining: drag a

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: allow, area, businesses, cannot, cards (+5 more)

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, when a competitive game against the AI ends (e.g. I win
because the AI goes bankrupt) and I click **[ Play Again ]**, the new match must
start completely fresh and must not be decided on its opening day: no seat
carries over any wallet, elimination flag, hand, staff or score from the
finished run, and the AI cannot be bankrupt on the first turn of the new game.

# Reported behaviour (repro)

1. Play a competitive game (human vs AI).
2. Win: the AI seat goes bankrupt and the game-over overlay appears.
3. Click **[ Play Again ]** and start a new game.
4. The AI is bankrupt again — reported as "went bankrupt in the first turn".
   The reporter's hypothesis: "their stats were not reset".

# Root cause (investigation)

The reporter's hypothesis was **wrong about the mechanism**, but the symptom is
real and reproducible.

- **The Play Again / New Game path is clean.** `createCompetitiveState()` seeds
  every `PlayerRecord` from the difficulty preset (Medium: 600 coins / 300 rep,
  `eliminated` unset, empty hand/staff, score 0). Verified by simulation: new
  games after a finished run always started with fresh seats.
- **The real defect is an opening-day elimination.** Competitive AI seats are
  driven by the single-player `Greedy` / `BankingGreedy` strategies, which spend
  freely down to the last coin — e.g. hiring 400 of the 600 starting coins on
  turn 1. The shared closing then applies the day's incident (a flat `-200`
  Protest, `-500` General Strike, or an accepted dual-choice option) to a wallet
  that can no longer absorb it, so the seat goes negative and is **eliminated on
  turn 1**. With one AI opponent that immediately ends the match
  (`last_standing` / bankruptcy), so the player sees "the AI went bankrupt in
  the first turn" right after Play Again. Measured on 80 seeds per
  strategy/difficulty combination, 1–5 % of *first-ever* games were decided on
  turn 1 this way (two reproduced failure seeds are pinned in the regression
  test as `dayone-12` and `dayone-42`).

# Scope

In scope:

- Competitive opening-day solvency (no seat can be bankrupted on turn 1).
- AI seat liquidity: AI seats keep a difficulty-gated reserve instead of
  spending their last coins.
- Regression coverage for both, plus a guard that a new game after a finished
  run starts from fresh seats.
- Game rules documentation.

Out of scope:

- AI strategy strength / balance tuning beyond the liquidity floor.
- Single-player loss conditions (unchanged: bankruptcy can still end a
  single-player game on turn 1).
- Changing incident card values or the shared incident deck.

# Acceptance criteria

1. **Fresh seats on a new competitive game.** Creating a competitive game after
   a finished one yields every `PlayerRecord` at the preset's starting
   coins/reputation with `eliminated` unset, empty hand/staff, score 0 and no
   failure badges. *Metric: automated test after a played run whose AI seat is
   left bankrupt/eliminated.*
2. **The opening day cannot be decided by debt.** A competitive seat that would
   end turn 1 with negative coins has its debt written off to 0 (logged as
   `First-day grace: …`) and is not eliminated; no bankruptcy game-over is
   declared on turn 1. *Metric: unit test of `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`
   plus the two reproduced day-1 failure seeds (`dayone-12`, `dayone-42`) still
   running at turn 2 with both seats solvent.*
3. **Bankruptcy elimination is unchanged from turn 2.** A negative seat from
   turn 2 onwards still fails `checkCompetitiveSeatFailure` and is eliminated
   exactly as before. *Metric: unit test.*
4. **AI seats keep a liquidity reserve.** `competitiveAiReserveCoins` is
   difficulty-gated (Easy 50 %, Medium 35 %, Hard 25 % of the preset's starting
   coins); a bound AI seat sees only its spendable balance, restores exactly the
   withheld reserve (never charged), and an AI MarketPhase never takes the seat
   below its reserve. *Metric: automated tests + a full AI MarketPhase across
   several seeds.*
5. **Single-player unchanged.** The grace is inert without a `players[]` roster
   and single-player bankruptcy still applies on any turn. *Metric: unit test
   plus the existing suite.*

# Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngine.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-play-again-reset.test.ts`

# Assumptions (documented for the producer)

- Because incidents are drawn from the shared deck and their size is outside a
  seat's control, a liquidity reserve alone cannot guarantee the AI will not be
  bankrupted on the opening day (`-500` General Strike vs a 600-coin purse), so
  a **symmetric turn-1 solvency grace** is applied to every competitive seat.
  It mirrors the pre-existing turn-1 grace for reputation collapse, and it
  changes competitive play only; single-player keeps its rules.
- The reserve is applied in the interactive AI driver only. Headless harnesses,
  Monte Carlo balance runs and the human seat are unaffected, so the balance
  baseline gate is untouched by design.

During the implement gate for MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 (three finish attempts), the browser suite command
`npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` failed intermittently while the host was CPU-saturated (load average 20-58 from concurrent agent test suites across repos):

- `allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal` — `Timed out waiting for turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation after 15000ms` (the test took 25.9s vs a normal ~2-10s).
- `only materializes purchased cards at destination after transfer animation completes` — `Timed out waiting for business bought to hand after 6000ms`.

Both are single-player scene tests unrelated to that change, and both pass on a quiet machine (20/20 in 51-69s). Root cause is the tight fixed waits in `waitForCondition` racing the framed Phaser income/presentation animations (the income-collection deferral has a 16 s safety cap, which exceeds the 15 s test wait) when requestAnimationFrame is starved.

Suggested options (producer decision): (a) derive the two waits from the animator's bounded caps, (b) force reduced motion / headless pacing in these tests, or (c) accept as a known flake and document the retry expectation.

# Intake Brief — `unit-cli` project is silently skipped by `npm test`

## Problem statement

`npm test` (the retry runner invoking `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli`)
regularly executes only the `unit` project: none of the five serialized CLI files in
`CLI_TEST_FILES` are collected, no `|unit-cli|` lines are reported, and the run is still
green. The Playwright-driven `storyline-graph-svg` render/doc-drift guard and the four
storyline/harness CLI suites therefore run in some full-suite runs and not in others, so a
green gate does not mean everything ran.

## Users

- **Implementer / agent** running the changed-scope or full-suite gate before committing —
  needs "green" to mean "every non-browser test file ran".
- **Reviewer / auditor** reading a cached gate result (`.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt`) —
  needs the run's coverage to be reproducible for a given commit.
- **Release engineer** promoting `dev` → `main` — needs the gate evidence to be trustworthy.

### User stories

- As an implementer, when the gate reports green I want evidence that every configured
  project contributed its files, so a CLI-test regression cannot slip through unnoticed.
- As an auditor, I want a green cached run to be reproducible — the same commit must not
  sometimes exercise 375 files and sometimes 380.

## Evidence (verified during intake, 2026-10-23)

- `HEAD` = `582ab9e5` holds **380** non-browser `*.test.ts` files; `CLI_TEST_FILES` in
  `vite.config.ts` holds **5**.
- The most recent cached full run (`5cb02674`, 2026-10-23 11:09Z, exit 0) reports
  `Test Files 375 passed (375)` and contains **zero** occurrences of any of the five CLI
  file names — exactly the 5 CLI files are missing and `unit-cli` contributed nothing.
  Same shape in `6edb5947` (371), `6773e550` (370), `abb42afc` (365), `091fb66e` (373).
- **Arg forwarding is not the cause.** The runner's own diagnostic in a skipping run reads
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=2 status=0 outcome=accepted-transient args="--project unit --project unit-cli"`;
  both retry attempts skipped the project identically, so it is not a transient-teardown
  artefact and not a lost flag.
- **Not a persistent config regression.** The identical main checkout ran `unit-cli`
  successfully at 2026-10-22 16:49Z (`7b5c9894`, five `|unit-cli|` lines) between two runs
  that did not (21:10Z `6edb5947`, 21:53Z `6773e550`). Every run reports
  `RUN v3.2.7 /home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`.
- **Block structure suggests state, not source:** every run up to 2026-10-18 01:21Z shows
  `|unit-cli|`; runs from 2026-10-19 21:21Z on mostly do not — yet no commit touched
  `vite.config.ts` or `package.json` between `a2a25864` (2026-10-18 01:17Z) and
  `866294b5` (2026-10-20 01:02Z).
- The existing guard `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` asserts the
  **declared** config shape (project names, `include`/`exclude`, serialization flags) but
  not the **run-time project selection**, which is precisely why it stays green while the
  project is skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Root cause identified and fixed at the cause — the work item records which hypothesis
   (H1 zero-file collection, H2 project filtered out, H3 stale environment state, or another)
   was confirmed, with the evidence that confirmed it; if the cause proves to be a Vitest
   defect, it is documented in the item as an upstream issue rather than papered over.
2. `npm test` deterministically executes all five `CLI_TEST_FILES` in a **single** Vitest
   invocation (both `--project` flags retained — no additional invocation stage): proof is a
   full-suite run containing `|unit-cli|` lines for every one of them (or an equivalent
   machine-checkable record, e.g. JSON-reporter entries with `projectName: unit-cli`), and the
   item records the measured before/after suite duration showing no meaningful increase.
3. A run in which a configured project contributes **zero** test files fails loudly instead
   of reporting green, naming the empty project and its expected files.
4. A regression test pins the run-time selection for the `npm test` argument set: `unit` and
   `unit-cli` are both resolved, every non-browser `tests/**/*.test.ts` file is claimed by
   exactly one project, and the five CLI files are claimed only by `unit-cli` (fast static
   check that runs in the `unit` project).
5. `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the deterministic invocation, the zero-file guard and the
   intermittent-skip symptom, including what a green full-suite run must contain.
6. Full project test suite passes with the changes (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- **Fix the quirk, do not route around it** (producer decision, 2026-10-23): keep the single
  `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation and repair the project-selection
  behaviour at its cause. Adding a second invocation stage is acceptable only if the root
  cause proves unfixable — and the resulting wall-clock cost must then be measured and
  reported back to the producer.
- **Preserve MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG isolation.** The five CLI files must not return to the
  parallel `unit` pool; they flake under file-level parallelism (spurious
  `expected 1 to be +0`).
- **Repository boundary.** `core/` is the engine submodule: `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`
  and `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` belong to the engine repo. Prefer a fix that
  lives in this repo (`package.json` script, `vite.config.ts`, a local wrapper, tests).
  If an engine-side change proves necessary, **raise it as a separate item in
  `../ContextHub`** (producer instruction, 2026-10-23) rather than bundling it here; an
  engine change also needs its own `engine:sync`/pin discipline. Note for the implementer:
  `./core` resolves to `../Tableau-Card-Engine`, while `../ContextHub` is the Worklog (`wl`)
  tooling repo — confirm the target repository at that point if the distinction matters.
- **`vite.config.ts` is auto-generated** from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, and that
  template does **not** carry `CLI_TEST_FILES`/`unit-cli`. Keep local edits surgical and
  documented so a future re-scaffold does not silently drop them (precedent:
  MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY applied a surgical sync for the same reason).
- Keep `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` semantics intact: retry-once on transient contention
  signatures, never retry a hang, never mask a genuine failure.
- Do not weaken the masking guard in order to make the gate green.

- `package.json`: `test` and `test:unit` both run

  `--project` filter, and it is kept but contributes no specs when its `include` matches
  nothing — neither produces a failure on its own.
- Two guards exist: `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` (config shape)

**Route (producer decision, 2026-10-23): diagnose and fix the quirk itself.** Keep the single
`vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation; do not add a second invocation
stage unless the root cause proves unfixable, and if it does, measure and report the added
wall-clock cost.

Diagnose, in this order (cheapest discriminating evidence first):

- **H1 — zero-file collection.** The `unit-cli` project initialises but its `include` matches
  nothing (root / `include` resolution inside an `extends: true` project), and Vitest reports
  green for a project that contributed no files.
- **H2 — project filtered out.** `VitestFilteredOutProjectError` drops the project because
  the effective `--project` name filter does not match the declared name

- explicit `root` on the `unit-cli` project (removes dependence on inherited root

## Verification and final state (commits `f9609f8d`, `f90bc263`)

**Root cause (AC1): H4.** Documented in the diagnosis comment above and in `docs/dev/testing.md`; it is an upstream Vitest 3.2.7 defect (its `sequence.groupOrder` group loop aborts on a rejected pool run and drops the remaining groups, still summarising the executed files as green), not an engine defect — nothing under `core/` was modified.

**AC2 — deterministic single invocation.** `npm test` is still one Vitest invocation with both `--project` flags. Evidence: the full-suite run at `de02c9c3` (which contains `f90bc263`) reported `Test Files 382 passed (382)` **with 5 `|unit-cli|` lines in BOTH attempts** (`\[vitest-runner\] attempts=2 status=0 outcome=accepted-transient`, cache `46053dd9`). Duration 200.89s / 191.55s (host load ~6-12) vs the pre-change cached range 166.62–232.08s — no meaningful increase (the change reorders two already-serialized groups and adds one ~0.3s wrapper process). The CLI stage itself is unchanged (5 files, same timeouts); the earlier 305.58s reading was host contention (load 33, summed test time +75%), not this change.

**AC3 — loud zero-file failure, now un-maskable.** Two layers: (a) the config-level reporter (`tests/tooling/vitest-project-coverage-reporter.ts`) compares scheduled (`onTestRunStart`) vs executed (`onTestRunEnd`) files per project, prints `[project-coverage-guard] FAIL` naming the project and every unexecuted file, and sets a non-zero exit; (b) `scripts/run-tests.ts` (the new `npm test`/`test:unit` entry point) runs the engine retry runner **once** (all args forwarded, no second invocation) and then enforces the reporter's machine-readable verdict, so a run the retry runner accepted as `accepted-transient` fails when its verdict is incomplete. A green run with no verdict also fails, so `--reporter=` cannot silently disable the guard. Proven against the real observed defect: on 2026-10-23 a retried run executed 0 of 376 `unit` files and was accepted; that is now a gate failure.

**AC4 — regression tests.** `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` pins the `npm test` argument set (both projects, exactly one invocation, retry timeout retained), the group ordering (`unit-cli` before `unit`), the on-disk file partition (every non-browser file claimed exactly once), the CLI-only claim, the exported `CLI_TEST_FILES", and the reporter wiring. `tests/tooling/vitest-project-coverage-reporter.test.ts` and `tests/tooling/run-tests-guard.test.ts` cover the verbatim guard behaviour (zero-file, partial drop, filter-aware expectations, verdict writing) and the wrapper's real exit-code behaviour.

**AC5 — docs.** `docs/dev/testing.md` now documents the deterministic invocation chain, why the CLI group runs first (with the symptom and the evidence), the zero-coverage guard and its output, the verdict enforcement table, and what a green full-suite run must contain.

**AC6 — full suite green**: `/skill:test` full scope at `de02c9c3` (contains `f90bc263`) → `success: true`, 382 files, 0 failures.

**Assumptions recorded:** filtered runs (`--project browser <file>`, `--changed`, `--shard`) stay quiet because expectations come from the run's own specifications; `npm test`'s own contract (invoke the wrapper, never `--reporter=`) is pinned by the AC4 test and documented.
